summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 2024.0: Fruncido Welcome to another video dedicated to the new functions of the 2024 version. This time, we will cover **fruncido**. ## What is Fruncido? Fruncido refers to the small wrinkles in the garment caused by the difference in tension between the fabric and the thread. As a result, we can see wrinkles wherever there are seams or bumps. The fruncido is more visible in denim. If you look at the denim clothes in Connect, you will see a variety of fruncido effects where there are stitches. Depending on the washing of the garment, the fruncido can be stronger or weaker. Fruncido is not limited to denim; you can also find it in your own informal designs. This effect can also be achieved by densifying the fabric to make it look more realistic. You can use normal maps and textures to maintain this appearance and modify the pattern. ## Accessing the Fruncido Tool Let's take a look at the fruncido function. The fruncido tools are found in the toolbar of the pattern window, where you can also select the materials in the main menu. Fruncido, as well as **pespunte**, has a separate window to manage its style, which is selected in the window selection menu. You can activate and deactivate the generated fruncido in the window display menu. Additionally, you can select the fruncido tool in both the 2D and 3D windows. When the fruncido tool is selected in the 2D window, the fruncido line is shown in purple. ## Overview of Fruncido Tools In the toolbar of the 2D window pattern, you will find a group of fruncido tools along with pespunte tools. There are four tools in total: 1. **Edit Fruncido** 2. **Fruncido Segment** 3. **Fruncido Free** 4. **Fruncido Sewing** Similar to the pespunte tools, let's use the fruncido tool in a simple pattern. The file is added at the bottom of the video. ### Using the Fruncido Tools - The **Fruncido Segment** tool creates wrinkles in only one line segment. If you create fruncido on a symmetrical pattern, it will be created in all symmetrical patterns. - The **Fruncido Free** tool creates a free line on top of a line segment, regardless of where the cubes are located. The first click will start the fruncido, and the second click will end it. - **Fruncido Sewing** is generated on both sides of a sewing line by clicking on it. - The **Edit Fruncido** tool allows you to select a created fruncido and move the entire line segment or a point. Note that fruncidos cannot be created by overlapping or other fruncidos. ## Fruncido Properties Next, let's take a look at the fruncido properties. Create a fruncido segment in a pocket. When you select the created fruncido, the properties of the fruncido object are available in the properties editor. You can name the fruncido, choose a style, configure extend, and configure displacement. - **Extending** is an option to extend the end of the fruncido generated to the outline of the pattern. If you deactivate the configuration extend (start, end) in the properties window, you will see that the fruncido is generated at a straight angle with respect to the line segment. - The adjustment of **displacement** refers to the distance between the beginning of the fruncido and the outline of the pattern. Displacement in Z applies a displacement in Z only to the texture of the fruncido, which can be useful if the fruncido and the pespunte in OBJ are superimposed. It is used to prevent the pespunte from covering the fruncido. For the sewing line of the fruncido, the property of the object has a location. It will be created on both sides of the union line in a predetermined way. It can be adjusted with the option A, B, or both in the positioning menu. If it is creating fruncidos in an inner shape, it can change to the other side of the inner shape through the **flip menu** in object properties. ## Fruncido Window Overview You can find the fruncido window menu under the pespunte window in the window selection menu. It is organized similarly to the other object windows and has the buttons **add**, **copy**, **assign**, and **delete** not used in the upper part. The **Edit Fruncido** tool allows you to use an emergent menu when you right-click on a fruncido line. Options include: - **Select All with the Same Property**: Click a new fruncido, delete it, or select all objects that use the same style of fruncido. - **Assign to New Fruncido**: Register and add the selected fruncido lines as the new predetermined style. When you select a fruncido style, the properties of the fruncido style will appear in the properties editor. You can save and open the properties of the fruncido style in a `.ptp` file format. You can change the form of the fruncido with the types: cotton, denim, leather, nylon, and polyester material. In a predetermined form, the fruncido only uses a normal map, but you can add textures. The textures with transparency allow for greater variation in the appearance of the fruncido. Like any other texture, the normal map menu allows you to eliminate the color by saturation, and the normal maps can be adjusted with intensity. The color and opacity are only applied to the texture. ## Fruncido Density and Width In specifications, the **density** is the amount of density of the fruncido, representing its thickness. The **width** allows you to adjust the width of the fruncido. Since fruncido is often used together with pespunte, we will use it in parallel with the pespunte. ### Adding Fruncido to Pespunte There is a pespunte on the side. Let's add a fruncido to this pespunte. First, click on the side line with the fruncido segment tool. Then, in the fruncido window, select the fruncido style and increase the intensity of the normal map in the properties window. Observe how it sharpens. I want the fruncido to be closer to the pespunte line than to the predetermined sewing line. So, I use the **fruncido editing tool** to select the fruncido line. I am looking for a value of approximately 2, which overlaps slightly with the pespunte. Again, in the fruncido style properties, we leave the material as it is, which is Oxford cotton. To give it a very washed look, we add a texture. In the fruncido style properties, click on the open file button next to texture. In the route `assets-material-hardware and trims-hackering`, we select the texture cotton. Explaining a texture like this gives it a more discolored and whitish look. We reduce the density to make it lighter and adjust the width. In the fruncido window, you can see the fruncido lines that have already been created, so that they coincide with the pespunte. ### Setting Fruncido for Neckline and Armhole We set the fruncidos for the neckline and the armhole. We select the fruncido of double point and use the fruncido segment tool to create the fruncido. Select the created fruncido objects. We go to the properties window and adjust the displacement value so that the fruncido begins at the first pespunte. Don't forget to adjust to 31 by 1 to ensure the border line is aligned correctly. ## Conclusion That's it for the fruncido function, where you can modify your fruncido to achieve a good fit. Just click on the screen recognition button, go to files, and load your desired file. Back to our sketch, and you're all set! ```
